items.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: But now my initial influence I would say would have to be probably Illinois Jacquet. But I liked Lester Young, Gene Ammons, and I liked Stan Getz and I like Warne Marsh a lot

ctx.x: Well I liked everybody really, starting with Illinois Jacquet. And it’s funny, when you’re out of New York you get a better feel of what really — see being in the south I got all

those different influences, Gospel, blues — so I liked Tom Archia, you know, the guy who worked with Wynonie Harris, and then there was Johnny Griffin with Hot Lips, and other guys played in R&B things. Willis Jackson. And then I liked Hank Mobley, just everybody, I liked everybody. But now my initial influence I would say would have to be probably Illinois Jacquet. But I liked Lester Young, Gene Ammons, and I liked Stan Getz and I like Warne Marsh a lot, and I liked another saxophone player that used to be from…
People seem to associate you a lot with organ groups, but that’s only part of what you did.
